title: Antigravity Tri-Store Trinity: Ephemeral Runtime Archaeology and Visual Brief Preservation
author: Antigravity Book-to-Skill Forge (book-to-skill-forge)
context: The Antigravity IDE and Harness ecosystem partitions agent execution deliverables into an orthogonal Tri-Store Trinity: (1) Relational step execution database at conversations/*.db (mined by conversation-trajectory-miner); (2) Persistent workspace artifact store at brain/<cid>/ (mined by brain-artifact-miner); and (3) Ephemeral runtime and visual brief store at %TEMP% (C:\Users\spectre\AppData\Local\Temp\, mined by temp-artifact-miner). An empirical census of %TEMP% cataloged 133 HTML visual briefs (10.21 MB) spanning 16 cognitive domains, 23 interactive topology snapshots (406.5 KB each), and 3 pytest sandbox test environments.
distilled_learning: Preserving intellectual assets and runtime diagnostics from ephemeral stores requires four operational invariants: (1) Non-Modifying Read Hygiene (Rule 46) preventing destructive deletions of live proactor sockets or un-salvaged briefs; (2) Heavy Topology Context Bounding (Rule 9, 48) summarizing 400KB+ Cytoscape/SVG graphs to prevent context blowout; (3) Bounded Sandbox Traversal (Rule 52) inspecting pytest-of-spectre fixtures to depth <= 3 with noise root pruning; and (4) Dual-Lens Cognitive Bifurcation (Rule 41) committing visual decision records to the Knowledge Vault with cryptographic isnad verification.

claims.assertion: The Antigravity ecosystem maintains a Tri-Store Mining Trinity where %TEMP% serves as the ephemeral visual deliverable and sandbox store containing 133 interactive HTML visual briefs and 3 pytest test sandboxes.
Interactive visual topology snapshots (skill-graph-*.html) average 406.5 KB each and must be bounded via metadata summaries to prevent LLM context window blowout.

Ephemeral pytest sandbox fixtures in pytest-of-spectre/ maintain dynamic mock skill trees that require bounded directory traversal (depth <= 3) and noise root pruning to prevent proactor pipe deadlocks.
